title: Four analytics stores split by runtime: MemoryAnalyticsStore and KnexAnalyticsStore run everywhere, BrowserAnalyticsStore is browser-only and PostgresAnalyticsStore is server-only
content:
| Store | Browser | Node | Bun |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MemoryAnalyticsStore` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `BrowserAnalyticsStore` | ✅ | | |
| `KnexAnalyticsStore` | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| `PostgresAnalyticsStore` | | ✅ | ✅ |

Two of the four have behaviour worth knowing before choosing.

**`MemoryAnalyticsStore`** is in-memory by way of **a WASM build of Postgres — PGlite**. It requires an asynchronous `await store.init()` for two reasons: downloading and initialising the WASM build when no `PGlite` instance was supplied, and initialising the in-memory database's schema. The initialisation is **idempotent** (existing tables are not recreated), and — importantly — `init()` **is not on the `IAnalyticsStore` interface**, only on the concrete type, so a caller holding the interface cannot initialise it. Both `knex` and `pglite` objects can be passed in, which is how it shares a database with other consumers.

**`PostgresAnalyticsStore`** uses the `pg` package and **assumes a fully-initialised Postgres database already exists** — the opposite contract. It takes a connection string or a `knex` instance, and adds a `raw(sql: string)` method that is *not* on the interface and is explicitly "not intended for production use cases".

Both accept the same optional constructor extras for observability: `queryLogger`, `resultsLogger` and a `profiler`.
